chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Appearance, punctuality and the rhythm section as a machine
summary: Danny says he succeeded by keeping appearances, being on time and locking in with the bass, piano and drums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And I found all them other virtuosos, Banjo Bernie and all them kind of people who played, you know, all kind of fantastic banjo, and they was out there scufflin', you know? So I found out that you keep appearance and watch the clock and be on time. And that was my success, not that I was actually...you know... Because at that time you had to try and play a rhythm and try to work with a section. See, now, you can be a virtuoso... You wouldn't be no virtuoso, not in them bands, because you'd get fired. So you sat down with the bass player, the piano player and the drummer, you got together and you had a machine going there. And they had what you call very famous, popular rhythm sections. They would say, "Who is in the rhythm section?" Who was in McKinney's Cotton Pickers' rhythm section? Or who was in the rhythm section with Fletcher? And who was in the trumpet section with Charlie Johnson? You know, you had sections.
Who was in the trombone section...?
Oh yeah. You had to get into them cliques.
